beaconsoftware-beaconsoftware:ashbyhq:8a.description: TECH LEAD — TOOLHOUND (EMBEDDED, BEACON SOFTWARE) WHERE THE WORK IS Beacon buys great vertical software businesses and makes them dramatically more valuable, not by squeezing them, but by giving them world-class engineering and AI leadership they could never hire on their own. Our engineers go where the work is: embedded inside a single business, owning its technology end to end, and compounding its enterprise value quarter over quarter. This role is one of those seats. You will be the technical leader for ToolHound, a mature, profitable tool-and-asset-management platform used by industrial, construction, energy, and manufacturing customers to track where every tool and asset is, who has it, and what it costs them. You won't advise from the outside. You'll own the codebase, set the roadmap, lead the team, and be measured on the value you create. This is an AI-native rebuild, not maintenance. ToolHound is a profitable, established platform, and the mandate is to reimagine what it does with AI at the center, and you're the technical leader who owns that from the front. We're looking for a jack of all trades, a strong generalist who can go deep where it counts. Deep, current .NET expertise is the price of entry, because that's what ToolHound is built on today. Over time, ToolHound converges onto Beacon's shared engineering standards, and you'll be the one leading that journey. The right person is excited by both, mastering the stack in front of them and growing into a broader one. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Own the technical and product roadmap. Decide what gets built and why, in partnership with the GM and customers. Translate business priorities (retention, expansion, new verticals, operational leverage) into a sequenced engineering plan you're accountable for. - Drive everything technical. Architecture, code quality, security, data modeling, performance, release engineering, and the migration path. You set the bar and you'll make the final technical decision. - Ship AI that changes the business, not demos. Take the natural-language assistant and the broader AI surface from plan to production: evals, guardrails, tenant-safe tool use, and features customers feel. You know when to lean on a foundation model, when to fine-tune, and how to keep agentic workflows on the rails in a multi-tenant system. - Lead and grow the team. Mentor the current engineer, raise their ceiling, and establish the best practices. - Increase velocity and harden the codebase. Make shipping faster and safer: modernize the stack, tighten the SQL and data layer, invest in test coverage and automation, and pay down risk so the platform can carry far more weight than it does today. - Be the technical face of ToolHound. Earn the trust of operators and customers, set expectations, and communicate clearly in writing. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - A senior .NET expert — day one. Deep, current C# / ASP.NET http://ASP.NET Core (through .NET 8–10), comfortable owning a large, mature codebase immediately: reading it, fixing it, and reshaping it with judgment. This is the non-negotiable starting requirement. - A genuine generalist ("jack of all trades"). You're T-shaped, deep in .NET now, but you pick up new languages, stacks, and clouds quickly and enjoy it. You can move across web, mobile, data, infra, and AI without waiting for permission, and you're energized (not threatened) by converging onto TypeScript/React, Go, Python, and AWS over time. - Cloud and SQL depth. You've designed, deployed, and operated real systems in the cloud, and can model, query, tune, and reason about production databases. - Mobile fluency. Hands-on with cross-platform mobile: .NET MAUI (or Xamarin/ native, with the ability to go deep on MAUI), including scanning, camera, and offline sync. - AI-native engineering. You've shipped production software on foundation models (LLM tool use, retrieval, evals, guardrails), not just prototypes, and you have a point of view on doing it safely in a multi-tenant produc

cogentanalytics-cogentanalytics:lever:d1.description: Primary Role Summary The Automotive Technician is responsible for diagnosing, repairing, and maintaining customer vehicles safely, efficiently, and in accordance with manufacturer and company standards. The Technician plays a critical role in delivering quality repairs, identifying additional service opportunities, and ensuring an exceptional customer experience. The Automotive Technician serves as the technical expert within the shop, providing accurate inspections, quality workmanship, and professional recommendations that support customer safety, vehicle reliability, and company profitability. Key Responsibilities 1. Vehicle Diagnostics & Repair Perform vehicle inspections and diagnostic testing. Identify mechanical, electrical, drivability, and performance issues. Diagnose root causes and recommend corrective actions. Perform repairs according to manufacturer specifications and company standards. Complete maintenance services including brakes, tires, alignments, oil changes, suspension, batteries, and other vehicle systems. Verify repairs through testing and quality control procedures. 2. Inspection & Customer Recommendations Perform comprehensive vehicle inspections. Identify maintenance and repair opportunities. Document inspection findings accurately. Communicate repair recommendations clearly to Service Advisors. Support customer safety and preventative maintenance programs. Assist in maximizing vehicle reliability and customer satisfaction. 3. Productivity & Workflow Management Maintain efficient work habits and productivity levels. Complete assigned work within established labor times. Manage workflow and prioritize assignments effectively. Support overall shop throughput and scheduling objectives. Minimize delays and operational bottlenecks. 4. Quality Control & Workmanship Ensure repairs are completed correctly the first time. Follow shop quality control procedures. Conduct final inspections and testing prior to vehicle release. Minimize comeback repairs and warranty work. Maintain high standards of workmanship and professionalism. 5. Safety, Equipment & Facility Care Follow OSHA, EPA, and company safety requirements. Utilize tools, lifts, and diagnostic equipment properly. Maintain a clean and organized work area. Properly handle and dispose of hazardous materials. Report damaged equipment and safety concerns immediately. Protect customer vehicles and company assets. 6. Documentation & Communication Complete repair order notes accurately and thoroughly. Document diagnostic findings, repairs performed, and recommendations. Communicate effectively with Service Advisors and management. Maintain accurate labor and time records. Participate in production meetings and training activities. 7. Continuous Improvement & Training Stay current with automotive technology and repair procedures. Participate in technical training and certification programs. Develop advanced diagnostic and repair skills. Support mentorship and knowledge sharing within the shop. Promote a culture of professionalism and continuous improvement.

distro-distro:lever:df69df8c-f654-4603-b.description: Principal Infrastructure Engineer — Cloud, Systems & Automation About the Role PrismHR is the technology engine behind Vensure Employer Solutions, and the infrastructure underneath it — our Azure cloud environment, our Windows and Linux systems, and the automation and monitoring that keep it all running — has to be dependable. We're looking for a Principal Infrastructure Engineer to join a tight-knit, five-person infrastructure team responsible for day-to-day operations across our environment, not a single fixed project. Beyond the day-to-day, you'll be expected to take real ownership of significant initiatives as they come up — including an upcoming Windows Server 2025 upgrade and a database version upgrade. You'll be trusted to drive these forward independently, with minimal oversight. Why Communication Matters So Much for This Role We want to be upfront about something: the previous person in this role struggled with communication — not being direct in answers, not documenting work clearly, and going quiet during projects instead of staying engaged and visible. That created real problems for the team. So for this hire, clear and direct communication, solid written documentation, and staying engaged and visible throughout a project are treated as core requirements, not soft extras. What You'll Do • Own day-to-day infrastructure operations across a small, close-knit team — this is a hands-on operational role, not a narrowly scoped project assignment. • Design, manage, and troubleshoot cloud infrastructure in Azure, including networking, load balancing, and network segmentation. • Own disaster recovery readiness, including Azure Site Recovery configuration, testing, and failover. • Administer and maintain a primarily Windows environment (~70% of systems), along with Linux systems. • Maintain and extend configuration management using Puppet. • Manage containerized workloads using Docker, including Docker Swarm. • Support and improve monitoring using Zabbix and Grafana, with an eye toward future adoption of Prometheus and Azure Monitor. • Take ownership of major initiatives as they arise — including the upcoming Windows Server 2025 and database version upgrades — driving them from planning through execution. • Document your work clearly and consistently, and communicate progress, blockers, and decisions directly and proactively to the team. What We're Looking For • Clear, direct communication and sustained engagement — you give straight answers, document your work as you go, explain what you're doing and why, and stay visibly engaged throughout a project from start to finish. This is one of the most important things we're evaluating for this specific hire. • Strong Azure cloud infrastructure experience — networking, load balancing, and segmentation. Azure is our primary infrastructure environment, so this is a core requirement. AWS experience is a plus but not required. • Disaster recovery experience, ideally with Azure Site Recovery — this is close to a firm requirement given how central DR readiness is to this role. • Strong systems administration skills across Windows and Linux — with Windows prioritized, since roughly 70% of our systems run Windows. • Puppet experience — our current configuration management platform. Chef or Ansible experience is acceptable if you can demonstrate you can translate that experience to Puppet. • Strong Docker experience — particularly with Docker Swarm and Docker Community Edition. • Monitoring experience — Zabbix and Grafana experience is directly relevant; familiarity with Prometheus or Azure Monitor is a plus as we look to expand our monitoring stack. • Strong troubleshooting and documentation skills — both are considered highly important for this role. • Comfort owning significant initiatives independently — you'll be expected to drive major projects like upgrades forward with minimal hand-holding. • PEO, payroll, benefits, compliance, or tax systems experience is not required — general fam
